title: Optimal Rates for Adaptive Private $k$-PCA
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Our adaptive private method achieves far lower error than all baselines across dimension, eigengap, noise, sample size, and target rank.
layout: 2x3 grid of line plots, shared legend on top, shaded confidence bands
description: A shared legend at the top lists six methods with colored line markers: Adaptive Private Oja (blue), k-DP-PCA (orange), k-DP-Ojas (green), DP-Gauss-2 (red), DP-Gauss-1 (purple), DP-Power-Method (brown). Below are six line plots in a 2x3 grid, each with shaded 95% confidence bands. The top row shows subspace error (Frobenius norm of the difference between projection matrices) against dimension d, eigengap and noise level sigma (log scale). The bottom row shows error against sample size n on a log scale for d=200 and k=2, 5 and 10. Blue and orange curves stay low while the green, red, purple and brown baselines remain near the maximum error. In several panels blue sits slightly below orange. The eye goes to the blue curve at the bottom of each panel.
caption: Comparison of AdaDPO with baselines on the spiked covariance model. We plot the mean over 10 trials, with shaded regions representing 95% confidence intervals. We set ε = 1, δ = 0.01. For the top row figures we set k = 5.
abstract: Given $n$ i.i.d. random matrices $A_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ with common expectation $Î£$, the goal of \emph{Differentially Private Stochastic PCA} is to identify a $k$-dimensional subspace capturing the leading variance directions of $Î£$, while preserving differential privacy~(DP) for each individual sample $A_i$. \citet{dungler2025iterative} introduced \kdppca, the first algorithm to simultaneously (1) achieve sample complexity $n=\widetilde O(d)$ for sub-Gaussian data, (2) adapt its privacy noise to the intrinsic randomness of the data, and (3) extend seamlessly to any target dimension $k\le d$. However, its sample complexity has a suboptimal dependence on $k$. We propose the first algorithm that achieves optimal sample complexity in both $d$ and $k$, while retaining properties (2) and (3) of \kdppca. Additionally, prior utility guarantees require a minimum sample size with exponential dependence on the eigengap. Our method removes this dependence. It also improves the dependence on spectral parameters, matching known lower bounds for the spiked covariance model. Unlike deflation-based approaches like \kdppca, our algorithm updates the full $d\times k$ subspace jointly rather than one eigenvector at a time. This non-deflation structure simplifies the algorithm, reduces the number of hyper-parameters, and improves computational efficiency, particularly when using block linear algebra libraries.
